title: Agricultural liming is a carbon sink in the Mississippi River Basin.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the 27.2 MB Zenodo zip (CC-BY-4.0), 5,855 files. Read README: all GeoTIFFs are 1-degree grids, 70x26 cells, 1900-2015. Opened MRB_river_data.xlsx (64 annual rows, 1954 onward, Ca/Mg/SO4/NO3 mean and SD in mg/L), Raymond_2018.csv (100 annual rows of discharge and bicarbonate flux), Raymond_2018_processed.csv (116 rows), MRB_average_total_fluxes.xlsx (116 years x 74 columns; metadata sheet says 346 grid cells in the basin), and the SCEPTER (reactive-transport model) annual CO2 emissions CSV (116 rows x 22 scenario columns).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the gridded acidity and lime layers were reconstructed from USDA census and other upstream datasets, and the ~0.44 GtCO2 and ~90% realization figures. Did not open the GeoTIFFs (no rasterio installed); grid dimensions are from the README.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo zip downloaded without login, 27.2 MB, CC-BY-4.0 (checked).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The only measured outcome, the river's annual bicarbonate (dissolved carbonate) flux, is a column (fHCO3_TgCYr) in Raymond_2018.csv (checked). The CO2-removal values in the grids are model outputs, not measured labels.

a3_inputs_present.note: Annual acidity and lime inputs are present as GeoTIFF layers and as basin-total columns in MRB_average_total_fluxes.xlsx (checked).

a4_units_stated.note: Units appear in the column names (molH_ha_yr, TgC/yr, mg/L) and in the README table (checked).

a5_enough_rows.note: The measured target is one river outlet with 100 annual values (64 years for the other ions). The gridded layers give 346 cells x 116 years, but they hold no measured outcome per cell. Far below ~1,500 rows.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Tiny; any model runs on CPU.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 116 years (1900-2015) and the 1-degree grid match the README and data statement (checked).

a8_label_provenance.note: Every per-grid-cell outcome (soil CO2 emissions, lime-driven carbon removal in kgCDR/ha/yr) is SCEPTER reactive-transport model output computed from the same input layers, so learning it would just copy the model (circular). The gridded inputs are themselves reconstructions, not direct measurements.

backbone.name: none; tabular/gridded geoscience data with no matching pretrained biology backbone
backbone.licence: CC-BY-4.0 data; SCEPTER code on GitHub

integration.partner_dataset: USGS river water-quality records (e.g. NWIS) for sub-basin outlets
integration.join_key: station location / grid cell and year

honest_claim_h3: A model could at most fit one river's 100-year bicarbonate flux record from basin-total acidity and lime inputs, so the claim would rest on a single time series.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use yearly fertiliser, acid deposition and lime inputs across the Mississippi basin to predict how much carbonate the river carries to sea.
plain_idea.train_on: Basin-total annual acidity and lime inputs, 116 years (1900-2015), or 346 one-degree grid cells per year (checked).
plain_idea.predict: Annual river bicarbonate flux at the Lower Mississippi, measured from water chemistry and discharge (100 years, checked); per-cell values exist only as reactive-transport model outputs.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Carbon-accounting groups would want to know whether liming removes CO2, but one 100-point time series answers that better with the paper's mass balance than with machine learning.

label_elsewhere.sources: USGS water-quality monitoring stations measure river alkalinity at many US sites (known resource, not searched here).
label_elsewhere.why: More river stations could add rows, but building that table means constructing the label across sources, which this dataset does not provide.

ml_idea: Regress annual river bicarbonate export on lagged basin acidity and lime inputs; rejected because there are only 100 measured years and the per-cell labels are reactive-transport model output.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the 27 MB archive size; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count measured outcome rows: 100 annual river values (done, kills it).

verdict_reason: A5 and A8 fail. The only measured outcome is one river's 100-year bicarbonate record. Every per-grid-cell outcome is output from the SCEPTER reactive-transport model, built from the same inputs, so learning it would be circular. The data is also geoscience rather than biology, and no backbone fits it.
